Partial correlations between responses

Source: R/interpret.R
mc_partial_cor.Rd

Computes the between-response partial correlation matrix \(\rho_{ij\mid\mathrm{rest}} = -K_{ij}/\sqrt{K_{ii} K_{jj}}\) from the estimated precision matrix \(K_b = \Sigma_b^{-1}\) of the graph layer (Lauritzen, 1996). It is invariant to the scale of the Pearson residuals, and it is computed from fit$graph$K_b for both the GGM and the DAG layer. A zero entry signals the absence of second-order conditional association between two responses given the others, which coincides with conditional independence only under joint normality. In Gaussian-copula models, that interpretation applies only when the precision is estimated on the latent Gaussian scale.

Usage

mc_partial_cor(fit)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

Value

An \(R \times R\) matrix of partial correlations with unit diagonal, with the response names as dimnames.

References

Lauritzen, S. L. (1996). Graphical Models. Oxford University Press.

See also

mc_partial_cor_delta for standard errors and intervals, mc_get_graph, mc_plot_network.

Other graph interpretation: mc_get_graph(), mc_partial_cor_delta(), mc_plot_network()

Examples

set.seed(1); n <- 200; x <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = rnorm(n), y2 = rnorm(n), y3 = rnorm(n), x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x, y2~x, y3~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_partial_cor(f)
#>              y1          y2           y3
#> y1  1.000000000 -0.02507805 -0.005680059
#> y2 -0.025078050  1.00000000 -0.040235728
#> y3 -0.005680059 -0.04023573  1.000000000
